title: 68,245 Black Friday Ads, Taken Apart
headline: Median brand launched its Black Friday ads just 13 days out
take: Matching the default 50% off won't stand out; the open lane is leading with a free gift, which headlined only about 1 in 100 Black Friday ads.
quote: Last season, 50% was already the default, so the number alone won't stand out.

title: Openers and Closers: Your Ads Do Two Different Jobs
headline: One video ad opens 70% of journeys and closes just 3%
take: Judging on last click kills your openers; slower non-promo ads drive new customers and earn a 10 to 20% CPA bump, while promos get held tighter.
quote: Judge everything on last click and that video is the ad you cut.

title: Don’t Cut the Wrong Ads (Our Pre-BFCM Cut List)
headline: 70% of creatives should be cut before week two
take: Most ads don't deserve a second week, but the cut line must move with spend: $200 at an $80 CPA is still a test, $2,000 is a cut.
quote: Most ads don't deserve a second week.

title: Six Things Your Meta Funnel Is Telling You
headline: Your 1.8 million non-buying viewers feed sales three months out
take: Optimizing Meta for add to cart backfires: it sends window shoppers, so cart rate rises while conversion rate falls, which is why from-the-top rates beat step-to-step for performance.
quote: If you ask Meta to optimize for Add to Cart, your Add to Cart rate will shoot up, and your conversion rate will shoot down.

title: How Many Ads Should You Launch To Profitably Scale Meta?
headline: One new ad per $3,000 asks 1.4x what top accounts ship
take: His own $3k-per-ad rule demands more creative than the top quartile ships, yet the brands he sees scaling well hit it, through strategy and diversity rather than AI slop.
quote: So when you divide total spend by ad count, you're averaging a power law.

title: 8 Types of Attribution Every DTC Brand Should Know (And the 3 I Actually Use)
headline: Platforms claimed 1,050 conversions for a brand with 600 orders
take: AI-powered attribution tools are guessing: they run biased click data through a black box and produce precise-looking numbers that are no more accurate.
quote: Every platform is grading its own homework.

title: Your Best Customer Keeps Changing
headline: Half your top 20% of buyers drop out next year
take: Falling LTV during a scale push is the signature of growth working, so stop aiming at a fixed best-customer persona and target recurring buying moments instead.
quote: Stop asking who your best customer is.

title: AEO / GEO / AIEO
headline: AI traffic converts 42% better than analytics makes it look
take: Post-purchase survey data and return reason codes are the most underused asset in DTC, fuel for answer-engine content and ad creative alike.
quote: They arrive as a finalist, not as a browser.

title: The First Customer P&L
headline: A 6.0 blended MER can hide a 1.3 new-customer aMER
take: Blended MER is a rearview mirror: a brand can look healthy while every new customer loses money, and true CAC runs 20 to 30% above platform CPA.
quote: The 6.0 is a rearview mirror pointed at customers they bought two years ago.

title: How to Actually Get More New Customers from Facebook
headline: Why 50% of your Meta sales still come from past buyers
take: Skip awareness campaigns unless you are near $100k a day on Meta; put problem-first, top-of-funnel creative inside your conversion campaigns instead.
quote: You need top-of-funnel creative in your conversion campaigns.

title: The most boring email you'll get today (concept vs. angle, settled)
headline: If 20 ads collapse into 3 concepts, that's your real velocity
take: Headline, color and music swaps are not new concepts; Andromeda clusters them with the original, so only new concepts and angles earn fresh retrieval entries.
quote: Color and font variations are completely out.

title: What It Actually Costs to Reach 1,000 People
headline: The Super Bowl's $63 CPM is only 3 to 4x Meta's
take: The cheapest CPM is usually the worst buy because CPM ranks almost inversely to attention, so compare CPM only within a channel and judge on cost per outcome.
quote: The ranking by CPM is almost the inverse of the ranking by attention.

title: A winner is not a variable
headline: That failed channel test had under half a percent chance of winning
take: Most 'this channel doesn't work' verdicts are bad variable accounting: stacking new creative, channel and strategy multiplies the odds of a win below one percent.
quote: Learn from individual wins, learn from aggregate losses.

title: The 5 Marketing Quotes Worth Keeping
headline: Five marketing quotes worth keeping, and the famous one may be folklore
take: Since 99% of thruplay viewers won't buy directly, favor ads that spend those 15 seconds on selling points to new people over repeat promos.
quote: Don't market something people don't want (and don't ask me to do it either).

title: Struggling to Scale on Meta? Start With These 3 Charts
headline: Healthy hit rate: 10 to 15%; winners last 60 to 75 days
take: A hit rate above 15% is a warning, not a win: it means too few or too similar launches, so budget gets forced into ads instead of earned.
quote: You are not filling a library, you are refilling a leaking bucket.

title: I Built a Skill That One-Shots Animated Ads, Inside Claude. It’s Free.
headline: Free Claude skill makes an animated paper-style ad in 15 minutes
take: Novelty is a cheap lever most accounts ignore, so an imperfect one-shot AI animated ad is still worth a test slot.
quote: Novelty is a cheap lever most accounts ignore.

title: 100 Things to Check Before You Launch Your Next Ad
headline: 100 pre-launch checks, from hook rate to one ad per $3,000
take: Trust the data over your taste: ugly, phone-shot ads beat polished studio work more often than anyone admits, about 80 to 90% of the time in his experience.
quote: Ugly ads beat polished more often than anyone wants to admit

title: Stop Pasting Ad Reports Into ChatGPT
headline: Stop pasting ad reports into ChatGPT; let Claude write SQL
take: Pointing an LLM at huge ad exports breeds hallucination; put the data in a real database and have AI write SQL against it.
quote: Just don't split the middle and point claude at a huge spreadsheet.

title: 13 Ideas From the People I Actually Learn From in DTC
headline: 13 DTC ideas share one edge: the real number underneath
take: The tactics are mostly known; the edge is seeing the real number under the convenient one, from marginal CAC to paid credit hiding in organic.
quote: The edge is in seeing the real number under the convenient one.

title: The Offer Is the Cheapest Growth Lever You’re Not Pulling (A Framework)
headline: Two words cut a brand's CPA 78%: pull the offer lever
take: Price is the first objection people name and the last lever to test; a gift worth 25% of the order can cost 5 margin points, a 20% discount costs 20.
quote: Most operators will test 200 ways to say it before testing one change to what they're offering.

title: You Forgot About Prime Day (Here’s the 96-Hour Triage Plan)
headline: Prime Day in 96 hours: don't test anything new
take: Don't pull back DTC Meta spend for Prime Day; shopping intent rises everywhere, and pausing exits a huge window and resets learning.
quote: The brands that win Prime Day built their demand in March and April.

title: The DTC static ad system: what 67,852 ads across 106 brands actually look like.
headline: Statics are 64.8% of DTC ads; run 6 to 8 formats
take: Static is not a secondary format: some of the biggest Meta spenders, like SHEIN and Calvin Klein, run over 90% image ads.
quote: Creative diversity beats creative volume.

title: The DTC Meta Ads Tier List
headline: Founder story ads convert 30 to 50% higher, topping his tier list
take: Lookalikes and retargeting are mostly a waste in 2026, frequency capping is F tier, and nothing he has tested beats a founder who can sell on camera.
quote: Every hour you spend tuning frequency caps is an hour you didn't spend making a new ad.
